Italian scientist, born in Pisa in 1564, who turned the telescope on the sky and tested ideas about motion by experiment and measurement.

  • In 1609 and 1610 he built telescopes and saw the moons of Jupiter, the phases of Venus, mountains on the Moon and countless stars in the Milky Way.
  • He studied falling bodies and the pendulum, and showed that motion could be described with mathematics.
  • He argued openly that the Earth moves around the Sun, as Copernicus had proposed.

That last point brought him into conflict with the church. In 1633 the Roman Inquisition tried him over his book, the Dialogue Concerning the Two Chief World Systems. He was made to recant and spent the rest of his life under house arrest near Florence, in Tuscany. There he wrote his Two New Sciences, on motion and the strength of materials.

He died in 1642, the year Isaac Newton was born. He is often called a father of the Scientific Revolution and of modern physics.
sum: Italian scientist, born in Pisa in 1564, who turned the telescope on the sky and tested ideas about motion by experiment and measurement.
